title: Negative information questions with plural olla forms
summary: With plural persons, use me emme ole, te ette ole and he eivät ole after the question word: Miksi te ette ole kotona? Miksi te ette ole kotona? — Koska olemme koulussa.
targetSkills: Negative information questions with plural olla forms
prerequisiteSkills: Negative information questions with singular olla forms
objectives: Build a plural negative information question with emme, ette or eivät and ole.
Keep the group perspective correct when replying.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Plural means more than one in this grammatical pattern.
A stem is the part of a word to which an ending is attached.
The partitive is a word form used here for an amount, an action's object, or a substance or group description.
The inessive is the in-place form, answering where.
With plural persons, use me emme ole, te ette ole and he eivät ole after the question word: Miksi te ette ole kotona? (“Why aren't you at home?” addressed to a group). Ole stays unchanged.
keyPoints: Use ette or eivät after the question word, without an extra -ko/-kö ending.

sections.title: Answering the question
paragraphs: An addressed group replies with emme ole (“we are not”) when the reply is negative. An affirmative information answer still uses its ordinary affirmative verb: Olemme koulussa (“We are at school”). He refers to another group and keeps eivät ole in a negative reply about that group.
A natural short reply to “Miksi te ette ole kotona?” is “Koska olemme koulussa.” (“Because we are at school.”). Use the full reply when it makes the person, action or correction clearer.
The exercises show supporting Finnish words and their meanings when recalling them is not the task. Read the complete English meaning before choosing the question or answer form.
keyPoints: Match the negative verb to the reply's plural person and keep ole unchanged.

sections.title: Build the answer forms
paragraphs: Olemme means we are here. Olla has the we-form olemme: ole- + -mme.
ovat means are here. Olla has the irregular plural third-person form ovat.
emme means we do not here. Emme is the plural first-person negative verb.
ole means be here. After a present-tense negative verb, olla takes the unchanged form ole.
eivät means do not here. Eivät is the plural third-person negative verb.
keyPoints: Match the negative verb to the reply's plural person and keep ole unchanged.

Plural means more than one in this grammatical pattern. The partitive is a word form used here for an amount, an action's object, or a substance or group description. An addressed group replies with emme ole (“we are not”) when the reply is negative. An affirmative information answer still uses its ordinary affirmative verb: Olemme koulussa (“We are at school”). He refers to another group and keeps eivät ole in a negative reply about that group. The complete reply means “Because they are tired”.
This makes the reason negative. The requested reason is affirmative: keep olen, on, olemme or ovat even when the question contains a negative verb.
The subject in the because clause controls its verb: minä olen, hän on, me olemme, he ovat. Match that subject rather than copying the negative question’s person.
